title:
一、英譯中：請將下列英文句子翻譯成中文。（10 分）
Measuring the time taken for the release of goods also meets the concerns of trade circles regarding long delays in Customs clearance.
answer: 衡量貨物放行所需的時間，也回應了商界對於海關通關曠日廢時的關切。
hint:
句構拆解
  • Measuring the time taken for the release of goods：動名詞片語當主詞（衡量貨物放行所花費的時間）；taken for... 是過去分詞修飾 time。
  • also meets the concerns of trade circles：meet the concerns of＝回應……的關切（meet 在此是「滿足、回應」）。
  • regarding long delays in Customs clearance：regarding＝關於；Customs clearance＝海關通關。
關鍵詞
  • measure 衡量
  • release of goods 貨物放行
  • trade circles 商界、貿易界
  • Customs clearance 海關通關
  • delay 延誤
翻譯技巧
  • 英文用動名詞當主詞，中文可譯成「衡量……（這件事）」或直接以動作開頭。
  • meet the concerns 不要直譯「遇見關切」，譯「回應……的關切」。
  • long delays 譯「曠日廢時」或「嚴重延誤」，比「長時間延遲」自然。
易錯點
  • Customs 首字大寫指「海關」，不是「習俗」（customs）。
  • trade circles 是「商界」，不是「貿易圈圈」。

title:
二、中譯英：請將下列中文句子翻譯成英文。（15 分）
以往海關的工作主要包含了親手去檢查車輛、貨物和船隻，但是那些日子早就過去了。今日，在含有新科技和技術的一次勤務中，焦點會比較集中在資訊管理上。
answer: In the past, the work of customs mainly involved physically inspecting vehicles, goods, and ships, but those days are long gone. Today, in an operation that incorporates new technologies, the focus is more on information management.
hint:
句構策略
  • 原文兩句，英文也建議兩句：①過去親手檢查＋那些日子已過去；②今日焦點在資訊管理。
  • 「以往海關的工作主要包含了親手去檢查……」→ In the past, the work of customs mainly involved physically inspecting...（involve + V-ing）。
  • 「那些日子早就過去了」→ those days are long gone（固定說法）。
  • 「在含有新科技和技術的一次勤務中」→ in an operation that incorporates new technologies。
  • 「焦點會比較集中在資訊管理上」→ the focus is more on information management。
關鍵詞
  • 海關 customs
  • 親手 physically／in person
  • 檢查 inspect／examine
  • 船隻 vessels／ships
  • 勤務 operation／duty
  • 納入 incorporate
  • 資訊管理 information management
加分寫法
  • 「那些日子早就過去了」也可用 that era is over。
  • 「焦點在」也可用 the emphasis has shifted to，更強調轉變。
易錯點
  • 「親手去檢查」不要逐字譯 check by hand，用 physically inspect。
  • 「一次勤務」不是 one time duty，用 an operation 較自然。

title:
三、英文作文：（25 分）
Write an essay of NO MORE THAN 300 words on the following passage. Do you agree or disagree with what the Customs officer did? Why or why not?
I went through customs on my way to a meeting. The Customs officer was very much interested in the bamboo blowgun I was carrying as a gift for my brother. He asked me if I had any darts for the blowgun, and upon receiving an affirmative answer, he asked if he could see them. I slid my hand into the gym bag and handed him a plastic cylinder with the darts inside. He asked what the dark stuff was at the points and I assured him it was poison but that the darts were safely sealed at both ends. He smiled and waved me on.
answer:
I disagree with what the officer did. A customs officer's job is to protect the border, and the passage describes a moment when the border was not protected.

The traveler declared, in plain words, that the dart tips carried poison. Whether or not the darts were sealed, poison is a hazardous material, and the officer had both the authority and the duty to examine the item properly—to identify the substance, check whether it was prohibited, and consult the relevant regulations. Instead he smiled and waved the traveler on. That smile is the problem: it turns a legal decision into a personal favor, and it tells every officer watching that a friendly traveler deserves less scrutiny.

One might argue that discretion is part of the job. Officers cannot inspect every bag thoroughly, and a sealed dart with a small amount of poison may pose little immediate risk. That is a reasonable point, but discretion should be exercised with a reason on the record—for example, after confirming that the quantity is below the threshold or that the item is permitted in checked baggage. A smile is not a reason.

There is also a practical consequence. If the traveler had been carrying something genuinely dangerous, the officer's decision would have been a serious failure. If the item was in fact legal, a short explanation would have taught the traveler what to declare next time.

Customs work depends on consistency. A single friendly wave-through may seem harmless, but multiplied across thousands of passengers it becomes a policy of not looking. The officer should have examined the darts, documented the decision, and then—if the law allowed—let the traveler go.
hint:
審題
  • 題目問「你同不同意這位海關人員的做法」，必須表態並說明理由；不是描述事件。
  • 字數上限 300 字（不是下限），建議 260–290 字。
  • 建議立場：不同意——毒鏢屬危險物品，僅微笑放行不符職責。
五段架構
  • 第一段（表態）：不同意；一句話點出海關的職責是保護邊境。
  • 第二段（理由一）：旅客已明說鏢尖有毒，屬危險物品；官員有權也有義務查驗、辨識、查法規，而不是微笑放行。
  • 第三段（讓步＋反駁）：承認裁量權存在，但裁量須有「記錄在案的理由」，不能只憑好感。
  • 第四段（後果）：若真是危險物品，就是嚴重失職；若合法，也該說明讓旅客下次知道如何申報。
  • 第五段（結論）：海關靠一致性；一次放行無害，累積千次就成了「不檢查」的政策。
關鍵詞彙
  • customs officer 海關人員；border protection 邊境保護
  • hazardous material 危險物品；poison 毒物
  • discretion 裁量權；scrutiny 詳細檢查
  • prohibited item 違禁品；declaration 申報
  • consistency 一致性；wave through 揮手放行
加分句型
  • A customs officer's job is to protect the border, and the passage describes a moment when the border was not protected.（破題）
  • That smile is the problem: it turns a legal decision into a personal favor.（比喻＋批判）
  • Discretion should be exercised with a reason on the record. A smile is not a reason.（短句鏗鏘）
  • Multiplied across thousands of passengers it becomes a policy of not looking.（分詞構句收束）
評分重點
  • 立場明確，且理由要從海關職責出發（不是泛談安全）。
  • 要有讓步段（承認裁量），才顯得不偏激。
  • 嚴格遵守 300 字上限。

title: A problem in the older boiling-water reactors would become disastrous because of a ______ safety system that houses the nuclear fuel.
hint:
1. A problem in the older boiling-water reactors would become disastrous because of a flawed safety system that houses the nuclear fuel.
（舊型沸水式反應爐一旦出問題，會因包覆核燃料的安全系統有缺陷而釀成災難。）
  • 考點：flawed＝有缺陷的（flaw 瑕疵）。
  • 線索：disastrous（災難性的）＋safety system（安全系統）→ 系統「有缺陷」。
  • 其他選項：lacking 缺乏的（be lacking in）；scraped 被刮傷的；throbbing 悸動的。
撇步
  • 系統、設計、論證「有瑕疵」→ flawed。

title: Other than being cold, hungry, and thirsty, John was in good condition, lucid, and speaking ______ when rescued from a blizzard.
hint:
2. Other than being cold, hungry, and thirsty, John was in good condition, lucid, and speaking coherently when rescued from a blizzard.
（除了又冷又餓又渴，約翰從暴風雪中被救出時狀況良好、意識清楚、說話條理分明。）
  • 考點：coherently＝條理清楚地、連貫地（形容詞 coherent）。
  • 線索：lucid（意識清楚）＋speaking ___ → 說話有條理。
  • 其他選項：approximately 大約；drastically 激烈地；significantly 顯著地。
撇步
  • 說話、論述「有條理」→ coherently；反義 incoherently。

title: Several reviewers considered Cooper's study to be well-designed and well-conducted, while others remained ______ about some of the data used in the study.
hint:
3. Several reviewers considered Cooper's study to be well-designed and well-conducted, while others remained skeptical about some of the data used in the study.
（幾位審查者認為 Cooper 的研究設計與執行都很完善，另一些人則對研究使用的部分資料持懷疑態度。）
  • 考點：be skeptical about＝對……存疑。
  • 句構：while 表對比（有人肯定 ↔ 有人懷疑）。
  • 其他選項：ambitious 有野心的；evasive 迴避的；pessimistic 悲觀的。
撇步
  • 對資料、說法「存疑」→ skeptical about。

title: Cape Town is so ______ that it rightly places high in any ranking of the most scenic big cities on the planet.
hint:
4. Cape Town is so gorgeous that it rightly places high in any ranking of the most scenic big cities on the planet.
（開普敦美得令人驚嘆，難怪在任何全球最美大城市排行中都名列前茅。）
  • 考點：gorgeous＝美麗的、令人驚嘆的。
  • 線索：most scenic big cities（最美的大城市）→ 美麗。
  • 其他選項：compatible 相容的；melancholy 憂鬱的；tentative 暫定的。
撇步
  • 風景、城市「美得驚人」→ gorgeous（近義：stunning、breathtaking）。

title: The government does not have to worry about the morality of the people; it is the people who need to be concerned with the ______ of the government.
hint:
5. The government does not have to worry about the morality of the people; it is the people who need to be concerned with the ethics of the government.
（政府不必擔心人民的道德；需要擔心政府倫理的是人民。）
  • 考點：ethics＝倫理（此處指政府的倫理、操守）。
  • 句構：
  • 其他選項：glamour 魅力；hunch 直覺；mentor 導師。
撇步
  • 政府、專業的「倫理」→ ethics；個人品德才是 morality。

title:
The United States in the sixties contains an affluent society within its borders. Millions and tens of millions enjoy the highest standard of life the world has ever known. This blessing is mixed. It is built upon a peculiarly    6    economy, one that often proliferates pseudo-needs rather than satisfying human needs. For some, it has resulted in a sense of spiritual emptiness, of alienation. Yet a man would be a fool to prefer hunger to    7   , and the material gains at least open up the possibility of a rich and full existence.

At the same time, the United States contains an underdeveloped nation, a culture of poverty. Its inhabitants do not suffer the extreme privation of the peasants of Asia or the tribesmen of Africa, yet the mechanism of the misery is    8   . They are beyond history, beyond progress, sunk in a paralyzing, maiming routine.

The new nations,    9   , have one advantage: poverty is so general and so extreme that it is the passion of the entire society to obliterate it. Every resource, every policy, is measured by its effect on the lowest and most    10   . There is a gigantic mobilization of the spirit of the society: aspiration becomes a national purpose that penetrates to every village and motivates a historic transformation.

subItems.hint:
6. It is built upon a peculiarly distorted economy, one that often proliferates pseudo-needs rather than satisfying human needs.
（它建立在一個特別扭曲的經濟之上，這種經濟往往製造偽需求，而非滿足人類真正的需要。）
  • 考點：distorted＝扭曲的（動詞 distort）。
  • 線索：proliferates pseudo-needs（製造偽需求）→ 經濟「扭曲」。
  • 其他選項：prosperous 繁榮的（與後文批評矛盾）；burgeoning 迅速成長的；multilateral 多邊的。
撇步
  • 後文接「偽需求」→ 前面一定是負面形容詞：distorted。

7. Yet a man would be a fool to prefer hunger to sanity, and the material gains at least open up the possibility of a rich and full existence.
（然而，寧願飢餓也不要理智的人是傻子；物質成果至少開啟了豐富完整生活的可能。）
  • 考點：sanity＝理智、神智健全（形容詞 sane）。
  • 句構：prefer A to B（寧願 A 而不願 B）→ prefer hunger to sanity＝寧可飢餓也不要理智（反諷）。
  • 其他選項：satiety 飽足；sagacity 睿智；sanctity 神聖。
撇步
  • 四個 s 開頭的選項：sanity 理智、satiety 飽足、sagacity 睿智、sanctity 神聖——記字根分辨。

8. Its inhabitants do not suffer the extreme privation of the peasants of Asia or the tribesmen of Africa, yet the mechanism of the misery is similar.
（當地居民雖不像亞洲農民或非洲部落那樣極度匱乏，但貧困的機制卻相似。）
  • 考點：similar＝相似的。
  • 線索：yet（然而）表轉折：程度不同，但「機制」相同。
  • 其他選項：different（與 yet 的讓步語氣不符）；insignificant 微不足道的；effective 有效的。
撇步
  • yet 前後對比：不像……那樣嚴重，但機制相似。

9. The new nations, however, have one advantage: poverty is so general and so extreme that it is the passion of the entire society to obliterate it.
（然而，新興國家有一個優勢：貧窮如此普遍而極端，以致消滅貧窮成為整個社會的熱情所在。）
  • 考點：however＝然而（插入語，置於主詞後、動詞前）。
  • 線索：前段講美國的貧困「機制相似」，此段轉談新興國家的「優勢」→ 轉折。
  • 其他選項：therefore 因此；moreover 此外；likewise 同樣地。
撇步
  • 段落轉向相反或新的面向 → however。

10. Every resource, every policy, is measured by its effect on the lowest and most impoverished.
（每一項資源、每一項政策，都以它對最底層、最貧困者的影響來衡量。）
  • 考點：impoverished＝貧困的（動詞 impoverish）。
  • 線索：the lowest（最底層）→ 最貧困的人。
  • 其他選項：infuriated 被激怒的；ingratiated 討好的；impersonalized 被非人格化的。
撇步
  • 貧窮的正式說法：impoverished（比 poor 正式）。

title: The technology for creating virtual advertisements has been around since 1995. Originally this type of advertising was used in sporting events. Virtual advertisements were placed where real advertisements would be distracting to players. For example, at a baseball game, the wall behind the batter and the umpire is called the backstop. Using computer technology, pictures of products and slogans can be drawn onto this wall and then broadcast during the game. Viewers of the game at home will see huge red and white advertisements for Coca-Cola plastered all across the backstop. But the pitcher in the stadium only sees the blank wall of the backstop. Advertisements can also be drawn by computers in the grass-covered center field at a soccer game or on the side of a virtual blimp drawn on the sky over the stadium.

subItems.title: 11. According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Virtual advertisements are more effective than real advertisements.
Virtual advertisements do not catch sports players' attention.
Both virtual and real advertisements get in sports players' way.
Virtual advertisements are only used in sports games.

subItems.hint:
→ Virtual advertisements do not catch sports players' attention.
（虛擬廣告不會引起運動員的注意。）
  • 定位：「Virtual advertisements were placed where real advertisements would be distracting to players... the pitcher in the stadium only sees the blank wall」
  • 推論：虛擬廣告只出現在轉播畫面，現場球員看不到 → 不會干擾球員。
  • 其他選項：(A) 文中未比較效果；(C) 真實廣告才會擋住球員；(D) 文中未說只用於運動賽事。
撇步
  • 細節題抓「only sees the blank wall」——現場球員看不到廣告。

subItems.title: 12. When virtual advertisements are used in a baseball game, who will see the ads on the backstop?
subItems.hint:
→ TV viewers at home.
（棒球賽的虛擬廣告，誰看得到？→ 在家看電視的觀眾。）
  • 定位：「Viewers of the game at home will see huge red and white advertisements... But the pitcher in the stadium only sees the blank wall.」
  • 其他選項：打者、裁判、投手都在現場，看到的是空白牆面。
撇步
  • 轉播 vs 現場的差別：viewers at home 看得到，現場看不到。

subItems.title: 13. What does the underlined word “blimp” in the passage mean?
subItems.hint:
→ Airship.
（blimp 是什麼意思？→ 飛船。）
  • 定位：「on the side of a virtual blimp drawn on the sky over the stadium」——在球場上空盤旋的物體。
  • 字義：blimp＝小型飛船、飛艇（airship 的一種）。
  • 其他選項：ceiling 天花板；star 星星；wall 牆。
撇步
  • 球場上空、可掛廣告 → airship / blimp。

title: Hilary Cash, a therapist based in Washington, first treated an Internet-obsessed patient six years ago; this makes her a veteran in the new field of cyberpsychology. Now she runs a clinic called Internet Computer Addiction Services for Web over-users. Many of her clients would qualify as genuine compulsives: men and women who spend so much time visiting chat rooms and porn sites that they become moody and secretive, stop sleeping, ignore their jobs and other responsibilities, lie to their loved ones, and lose interest in sex. If research presented to the American Psychological Association last year is correct, 6 percent of Internet users fit in this category. It may look like many of the clinic's clients are normal people who spend more time than their mates would like researching their family tree. Yet, to Cash and a growing number of experts, this type of computer habit is not without its potential dangers, especially for relationships. Researcher John Gottman of the University of Washington has found that marriages are more likely to be successful if partners spend at least six hours a week talking about day-to-day issues, dining out, and just doing couples of things. “That may only be five minutes at one time, half an hour at another, and a date once a week,” says Cash. “But once that critical time is lost, couples start to disconnect.”

subItems.title: 14. What kind of patients does Hilary Cash treat?

options.text: Couples who are starting to disconnect

subItems.hint:
→ People who are Internet-obsessed.
（Hilary Cash 治療哪類病人？→ 網路成癮者。）
  • 定位：「first treated an Internet-obsessed patient six years ago... runs a clinic called Internet Computer Addiction Services for Web over-users」。
  • 其他選項：夫妻關係問題只是「後果」之一，不是她治療的主要對象；(D) veteran 是指她自己是「老手」，不是病人。
撇步
  • 人物題回文找第一個描述：Internet-obsessed patient。

subItems.title: 15. According to the passage, what problem is NOT mentioned regarding people who spend too much time in cyberspace?
subItems.hint:
→ Stopping dining out.
（下列何者未被提及為網路成癮的問題？→ 停止外出用餐。）
  • 定位：文中列出的問題：moody and secretive、stop sleeping、ignore their jobs and other responsibilities、lie to their loved ones、lose interest in sex。
  • 陷阱：「dining out」出現在最後 Gottman 的建議（夫妻每週至少六小時聊天、外出用餐），那是解方，不是成癮者的問題。
  • 其他選項：忽略責任、情緒化與偷偷摸摸、對家人說謊——都在文中。
撇步
  • 否定題注意「出現在別處」的詞：dining out 是建議，不是症狀。

subItems.title: 16. What does the underlined word “compulsives” in the passage refer to?

options.text: People who are obsessive about something
People who visit chat rooms and porn sites
People who are moody and secretive
People who lose interest in sex

subItems.hint:
→ People who are obsessive about something.
（compulsives 指什麼？→ 對某事執著成癮的人。）
  • 定位：「Many of her clients would qualify as genuine compulsives: men and women who spend so much time...」
  • 推論：冒號後列出的行為（沉迷聊天室、色情網站）都是「強迫性、成癮」的表現，故 compulsives＝有強迫行為的人。
  • 其他選項：只是「症狀清單」中的單一項，不是定義。
撇步
  • 冒號後的清單是舉例，不是定義；定義要看前面的 general 詞（compulsive）。

subItems.title: 17. What does the underlined phrase “this category” refer to in the passage?
subItems.hint:
→ True compulsives.
（this category 指什麼？→ 真正的強迫症／成癮者。）
  • 定位：「Many of her clients would qualify as genuine compulsives... If research... is correct, 6 percent of Internet users fit in this category.」
  • 推論：this category 回指前一句的「genuine compulsives」。
  • 其他選項：APA 是機構；normal people 是對比；Internet users 是全體，範圍太大。
撇步
  • 指示詞回指：往前找最近的名詞片語（genuine compulsives）。

subItems.title: 18. According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Researchers have found that marriages are more likely to be successful if partners spend at least 6 hours a week visiting chat rooms.
Experts have found that spending too much time on the Internet can pose potential dangers to social relationships.
Dr. Cash started to treat Web over-users at Internet Computer Addiction Services six years ago.
Normal people would like to spend time researching their family tree on the Internet.

subItems.hint:
→ Experts have found that spending too much time on the Internet can pose potential dangers to social relationships.
（專家發現，花太多時間上網可能對人際關係造成潛在危險。）
  • 定位：「to Cash and a growing number of experts, this type of computer habit is not without its potential dangers, especially for relationships.」
  • 其他選項：(A) 六小時是「聊天、外出用餐」，不是「上聊天室」；(C) 她六年前治療第一位病患，診所不是六年前開的；(D) 文中只是舉「研究族譜」為例，不是說正常人喜歡。
撇步
  • 細節題注意「not without」雙重否定＝有危險。

title:
The student thieves on campus need to look out. With the emergence of a new website to help teachers catch student plagiarists, these student thieves on campus have every reason to get worried.

Some students actually research and write their term papers in the old-fashioned way.    19    To prevent collegiate copycats, two graduate students at the University of California at Berkeley have devised a program that compares a student's submission with every other term paper on the Web.

“We essentially search a hundred million web pages on the Internet, interfacing with the top 20 search engines,” said John Barrie, of www.plagiarism.com. “We also compare that with our local database of term papers.” Teachers who sign up can send their students' papers to the website.    20    “We code every sentence that was a word-for-word match with another sentence, either contained on the Internet or within our database,” Barrie said. David Presti, a U.C. Berkeley professor who teaches neurobiology, told his class he would use the program. Undaunted, numerous students plagiarized anyway. “We ran all 300 papers through the program and found 45 of them, or 15 percent of students, had cut and pasted significant amounts of material from various World Wide Web sites without citations,” Presti said.    21    They can show the instructors “that indeed they haven't got their material from the Internet or some other source,” Barrie said.

Competition is tough at prestigious universities like U.C. Berkeley. Some students welcome the Internet research watchdog, considering it a way to level the academic playing field. “I think it's justified academically. Plagiarizing is wrong,” one said.

options.text: Some universities are suing those companies that sell term papers over the Internet.
Others, however, just copy fake ones off the Internet and turn them in as their works.
Students falsely accused can have the opportunity to defend themselves.
The originality of the work, or lack thereof, becomes painfully clear within 24 hours.

subItems.hint:
19. → Others, however, just copy fake ones off the Internet and turn them in as their works.
（然而，另一些人只是從網路上複製假論文，當成自己的作業交出去。）
  • 定位：前句「Some students actually research and write their term papers in the old-fashioned way.」→ Some... 之後應接 Others, however... 的對比。
  • 選項契合：Some（自己寫）↔ Others（上網複製）形成對照，並引出後文的「防抄襲程式」。
  • 其他選項：suing companies（文中無）、falsely accused（屬 21）、originality within 24 hours（屬 20）。
撇步
  • Some... 後面幾乎就是 Others, however...。

options.text: While many students approve of going after the sellers of the term papers, others say the school should target the students.
The teachers want the federal courts to enforce a law banning the sale of term papers.
Students falsely accused can have the opportunity to defend themselves.
The originality of the work, or lack thereof, becomes painfully clear within 24 hours.

subItems.hint:
20. → The originality of the work, or lack thereof, becomes painfully clear within 24 hours.
（作品是否原創，或缺乏原創，二十四小時內就會清楚地無所遁形。）
  • 定位：前句「Teachers who sign up can send their students' papers to the website.」→ 空格應說明送出後會發生什麼。
  • 選項契合：「24 小時內就知道是否原創」正是送交網站後的結果。
  • 其他選項：student approval（文中後面才談）、federal courts（無）、falsely accused（屬 21）。
撇步
  • 空格後接 “We code every sentence...”，前面要先有「很快就有結果」的句子。

options.text: Some universities are suing those companies that sell term papers over the Internet.
Others, however, just copy fake ones off the Internet and turn them in as their works.
Students falsely accused can have the opportunity to defend themselves.
While many students approve of going after the sellers of the term papers, others say the school should target the students.

subItems.hint:
21. → Students falsely accused can have the opportunity to defend themselves.
（被誤指的學生有機會為自己辯護。）
  • 定位：後句「They can show the instructors 'that indeed they haven't got their material from the Internet...'」——They 指學生。
  • 選項契合：「被誤指者可以辯護」正好接上「他們可以證明自己沒有抄襲」。
  • 其他選項：suing companies（無）、copy fake ones（已用於 19）、students approve（後面段落才出現）。
撇步
  • 代名詞 They 指學生 → 前面必須先提到「學生」。

title: Coffee is not usually thought of as a health food, but a number of recent studies suggest that it can be a highly beneficial drink.    22    Among them is a systematic review of studies published in 2005 in The Journal of the American Medical Association, which concluded that habitual coffee consumption was associated with a lower risk of Type 2 diabetes.    23    According to the authors, coffee contains antioxidants that help control cell damage that can contribute to the development of the disease. It is also a source of chlorogenic acid, which has been shown in animal experiments to reduce glucose concentration.    24    Studies that looked at decaffeinated coffee alone found the same degree of risk reduction.    25    In a report that combined statistical data from many studies, researchers found that people who drank four to six cups of coffee a day had a 28 percent reduced risk of diabetes compared with people who drank two or fewer. Those who drank more than six had a 35 percent risk reduction.

options.text: Caffeine seems to have little to do with it.
The exact reason was not known, but the authors offered several explanations.
Researchers have found strong evidence that coffee reduces the risk of several serious ailments.
Researchers are surprised to learn that coffee is the major contributor of antioxidants.

subItems.hint:
22. → Researchers have found strong evidence that coffee reduces the risk of several serious ailments.
（研究者已找到強烈證據，顯示咖啡能降低數種嚴重疾病的風險。）
  • 定位：前句「a number of recent studies suggest that it can be a highly beneficial drink」；後句「Among them is a systematic review...」→ 空格應總括「多項研究」與「Among them」。
  • 其他選項：caffeine（屬 24）、exact reason（屬 23）、major contributor of antioxidants（過度推論）。
撇步
  • 後句有 Among them → 空格須先提到「多項研究／證據」。

options.text: Caffeine seems to have little to do with it.
The exact reason was not known, but the authors offered several explanations.
However, some experts believe that coffee drinking can have negative health consequences.
Researchers have found strong evidence that coffee reduces the risk of several serious ailments.

subItems.hint:
23. → The exact reason was not known, but the authors offered several explanations.
（確切原因不明，但作者提出了幾種解釋。）
  • 定位：前句剛說「較低的第二型糖尿病風險」；後句「According to the authors, coffee contains antioxidants...」→ 空格是「原因不明，但作者提出解釋」的過渡句。
  • 其他選項：caffeine（屬 24）、negative consequences／strong evidence（已用或不合）。
撇步
  • 後句 According to the authors → 前面要提「作者提出解釋」。

options.text: Caffeine seems to have little to do with it.
The exact reason was not known, but the authors offered several explanations.

24. → Caffeine seems to have little to do with it.
（咖啡因似乎與此關係不大。）
  • 定位：後句「Studies that looked at decaffeinated coffee alone found the same degree of risk reduction.」——無咖啡因咖啡也有效 → 咖啡因不是關鍵。
  • 其他選項：exact reason（已用於 23）、larger quantities（屬 25）、negative consequences（文中未提）。
撇步
  • 後句講「無咖啡因也有效」→ 前面正是「咖啡因無關」。
